title: ITR 2026: Senior Citizens Can Claim ₹50,000 Medical Deduction
description: Senior citizens (60 years and above) can claim a deduction of up to ₹50,000 under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act. This deduction is available for medical e.

faq.q: Who qualifies as a senior citizen for this deduction?
faq.a: An individual who is 60 years of age or more at any time during the previous financial year qualifies as a senior citizen for the purpose of Section 80D deduction.

faq.q: What types of medical expenses are covered under this provision?
faq.a: Covered expenses typically include doctor's consultation fees, diagnostic tests, medicines, and treatment costs. It's crucial to retain proper bills and receipts for all such expenditures.

faq.q: Can this deduction be claimed by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs who are senior citizens and have taxable income in India can also claim this deduction under Section 80D, provided they opt for the old tax regime.

faq.q: Is there a limit on cash payments for medical expenses?
faq.a: Generally, payments for medical expenses to claim this deduction should be made through non-cash modes. However, expenses for preventive health check-ups (up to ₹5,000 within the overall 80D limit) can be paid in cash.

faq.q: Can I claim this deduction for my dependent senior citizen parents?
faq.a: Yes, if you are an individual (not a senior citizen yourself) and your parents are senior citizens, you can claim a separate deduction of up to ₹50,000 for their health insurance premiums or medical expenses, provided you pay for them and they are dependent on you.

faq.q: What documents do I need to keep for this deduction?
faq.a: You should keep all original medical bills, pharmacy receipts, diagnostic reports, and proof of payment (bank statements, UPI transaction records) to substantiate your claim if required by the tax authorities.

faq.q: Does this deduction apply if I already have a basic health insurance policy?
faq.a: Yes, if you have a health insurance policy but your premiums are less than ₹50,000, you can claim the balance amount for actual medical expenses incurred, up to the overall limit of ₹50,000 for senior citizens.
